title: Short Stuff: The Sad, Strange Tale of Margaret Schilling
summary: Short Stuff episode on the tale of Margaret Schilling (transcript spells it "Shilling"), a 53-year-old patient who went missing from the Athens Lunatic Asylum in Athens, Ohio, on December 1, 1978, and was found dead about six weeks later, on January 12, 1979, in a closed fourth-floor room. Her body outline left a stain in the concrete floor that would not clean off. The hosts cover the hospital's history (opened 1874, closed 1993, Kirkbride-style design), the search, the death ruled heart failure, and a 2007 Ohio University biochemist study that found the cleaning attempts locked the grave wax (adipocere) into the concrete. They also mention a 2018 Preservation Works tour and a host's college friend's senior film project about the hospital.

segments.title: Opening
segments.summary: Hosts open the Short Stuff episode.

segments.title: Athens Lunatic Asylum and Kirkbride design
segments.summary: Chuck describes a student film project by Emily Sinobocan about the Athens asylum. Josh gives the hospital's history: opened 1874, ran until 1993, and built on the Kirkbride plan from Thomas Story Kirkbride's book.

segments.title: Margaret Schilling's background and disappearance
segments.summary: Chuck introduces Margaret Schilling, a 53-year-old patient allowed to roam the grounds freely. Josh notes that little is known about her and that details are speculative. She was not noticed missing at breakfast; the alarm was raised when she missed dinner on December 1, 1978.

segments.title: Code search begins
segments.summary: A code search is called for the missing patient across the large campus.

segments.title: Search, police, and discovery of body
segments.summary: Staff and police search without success; the hosts say she was likely in a closed fourth-floor room in a tower reached by a hidden stairway. She was found dead on January 12, 1979, about six weeks after going missing, reportedly after a smell led to her body.

segments.title: Death ruling and the body outline stain
segments.summary: Her clothes were found folded beside her. Her death was ruled heart failure, though the cause was uncertain. Her body's outline left a stain on the concrete floor that would not clean off, and the hosts explain that sun-heated windows enabled decomposition.

segments.title: 2007 study of the stain and grave wax
segments.summary: A 2007 Ohio University biochemist study found the stain was adipocere (grave wax). Cleaning with acidic products locked it into the concrete, creating a white silhouette with a darker outline that remains today.

segments.title: Access restrictions and Preservation Works
segments.summary: The room is closed to the public. Preservation Works toured the site in 2018 and suggested a respectful public visit. Chuck is skeptical; Josh notes the alternative is students breaking in.

segments.title: Campus ghost stories and closing thoughts
segments.summary: Emily had not heard of this specific story, though she knew other campus ghost stories. The hosts reflect on how the story is almost ready-made for a ghost tale.
